issue: The scope annotations that carry the figure's central caveat are set in small, low-contrast gray type, while the bold percentages dominate. A reader scanning the table can easily take '~7%', '~10%', '~23%', and '~33%' as comparable cross-model numbers and miss that the DeepSeek rows are single-token whole-model ratios while the GLM rows are per-layer/per-head ratios.
evidence: The table's main numbers are large and bold; the qualifying text ('single-token KV cache', 'single-token inference FLOPs', 'per-layer KV (BF16)', 'attention only per head / layer') is small gray text beneath each row. A reader can reasonably infer that each stage builds on or requires the previous one, which is the opposite of the intended claim.

figure: Figure A.4 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: The band 'Inside post-training (build-time)' is colored blue, which the legend defines as 'system-side', but post-training is a model-building process that shapes the weights and is conceptually model-side. figure: Figure A.5 — Shared weights do not remove executed work
issue: The legend says 'Dashed arrows = weight reuse', but dashed arrows are also used from each pass down to its iteration history cache. Those arrows represent cache/history state, not weight reuse. The same line style therefore carries two different meanings, and the legend does not define the cache-state meaning.

The legend at the bottom defines only 'Dashed arrows = weight reuse'.
acceptance_test: Weight reuse and history-cache state use visually distinct line styles, and the legend defines both; a reader can tell which dashed arrows mean weight reuse and which mean cache state.

The caption says 'A true exit omits later work'; the legend says 'dashed box = not executed'.
